chunks: They who called Shu'aib a liar (disappeared) as though they had never existed; and those who called Shu'aib a liar were the ones who were ruined!

key_terms.الْخَاسِرِينَ: The losers, those who suffer loss in this world and the hereafter.
key_terms.شُعَيْبًا: Shu'aib (peace be upon him), a prophet sent to the people of Madyan.
key_terms.كَأَن: As if, as though (used for simile or metaphor).

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'as though they had never existed' in the context of the people of Shu'aib?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores the principle of 'complete ruin' (fawt), where the disbelievers of Madyan not only lost their worldly prosperity but were erased from historical memory, serving as a paradigm for those who reject divine guidance. The phrase 'as if they had not existed' highlights the totality of their loss, reinforcing the Shia emphasis on the inevitability of divine justice against those who deny their prophets despite clear signs.
